reason: The sources fully support a compelling story with 16 dual-sourced claims about the Space Shuttle program, its mechanics, landings, and historical milestones.
story: When NASA's Space Shuttle launched vertically from Florida, its three main engines and twin Solid Rocket Boosters generated millions of pounds of thrust. Two minutes into flight, the solid boosters jettisoned to be recovered at sea and refurbished for reuse. Over 30 years and 135 missions between 1981 and 2011, five operational orbiters—Columbia, Challenger, Discovery, Atlantis, and Endeavour—built an extraordinary legacy. They deployed and serviced the Hubble Space Telescope, docked with Russia's Mir station, and assembled the International Space Station. Yet when returning to Earth, these spacecraft performed one of spaceflight's most daring feats. With their engines completely silent after the deorbit burn, the orbiters reentered the atmosphere—enduring scorching heat up to 3,000 degrees Fahrenheit—and dropped out of orbit to land on the runway as unpowered gliders.
angle: Space shuttles did not land using engine power, but reentered the atmosphere and touched down on the runway as completely unpowered gliders.

claims.claim: The Space Shuttle program conducted a total of 135 missions between 1981 and 2011.
Five operational space-flown orbiters were built for the program: Columbia, Challenger, Discovery, Atlantis, and Endeavour.
Enterprise was constructed as a prototype test vehicle that performed atmospheric glide tests but never launched into orbit.
Two space shuttles were destroyed in fatal accidents: Challenger in 1986 and Columbia in 2003.
A total of 14 astronauts were killed in the Challenger and Columbia disasters.
Space Shuttle Endeavour was built to replace Challenger following its destruction.
Space shuttle orbiters were originally designed for a minimum lifespan of 100 missions or 10 years.
Space shuttles successfully deployed and performed servicing missions on the Hubble Space Telescope.
The Solid Rocket Boosters operated alongside the main engines for the first two minutes of flight before jettisoning.
Jettisoned Solid Rocket Boosters descended into the Atlantic Ocean by parachute and were recovered by ships for refurbishment.
Mercury astronaut John Glenn returned to space aboard Space Shuttle Discovery on mission STS-95.
The final space shuttle mission was STS-135, flown by orbiter Atlantis in July 2011.
Thermal protection tiles on the orbiter experienced temperatures reaching up to 3,000 degrees Fahrenheit during reentry.
Space shuttles docked with both Russia's Mir space station and the International Space Station.
The maximum number of crew members flown on a single space shuttle mission was eight.
Edwards Air Force Base in California served as a primary landing site for space shuttle missions.

disputed: Early shuttle mission catastrophic failure risk estimates varied dramatically: NASA management originally cited 1 in 100,000, engineer Richard Feynman estimated 1 in 100, while a later NASA retrospective study pegged the risk for the first nine flights at 1 in 10 (attribute according to retrospective NASA study).
